items.title: GO trains won’t run on these days in Mississauga and parts of Toronto
items.summary: GO trains won’t run this weekend along the normally busy Lakeshore West line in Mississauga, Oakville, Burlington and west Toronto, transit officials say. Metrolinx, the provincial agency in charge of GO Transit, said in an email update Wednesday morning work crews will be completing “major track upgrades” from early Saturday through end of the day on Sunday. “During this time, regular Lakeshore West train service will only run between Niagara Falls and Aldershot GO (in Burlington). ” Transit officials also noted the work will impact some late Friday night service as well. During the temporary shutdown of GO train service: Metrolinx further noted that ongoing construction from Oct. 23-26 at the Long Branch GO station in Toronto’s west end will also impact GO Transit customers. “There is no pedestrian or station access. Additionally, the parking lot will be closed due to construction. Please use Port Credit GO or Mimico GO,” transit officials said.

items.title: New Record: Huge estate sets record for most expensive house ever sold in Mississauga
items.summary: A luxurious private estate that just changed hands has officially broken the record for the most expensive home sold not just in Mississauga, but across the entire Region of Peel. Today, Sam McDadi Real Estate Brokerage announced it broke its own record with the city and region’s highest residential sale in history. 1 million, which was set at the Saint George Mansion (2275 Doulton Drive). “It’s been off-market for several months and I had an internal buyer who was quite interested, and we ended up getting two offers,” Sam McDadi told INSAUGA Canada. “It set a record for pricing that’s similar to the Bridal Path, which is great for our city,” he added, referring to the ultra-affluent Toronto neighbourhood that’s famously home to Drake and other well-known Canadian artists and moguls. Following on the heels of the Saint George Mansion, the multi-million-dollar sale is, McDadi says, a sign that Mississauga is a city that luxury homebuilders and buyers should pay attention to. ’’ While McDadi’s team says the exact price and address aren’t being revealed at this time, McDadi can share that the property, massive in size and full of rare amenities, has a special feel. “The architectural design and layout are fantastic. When you walk in there, you realize you have a special property,” he says, adding that the house is relatively new and was custom-built with top-notch touches.

items.title: CYMAT TO WELCOME GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS AND STRATEGIC PARTNERS TO ITS MISSISSAUGA FACTORY ON OCTOBER 28
items.summary: MISSISSAUGA, ON, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cymat Technologies Ltd. m. m. EDST (the "Event"). Following the Event, Cymat expects to issue a public announcement providing further details of the Event. Federal and provincial government officials, representatives of certain of Cymat's existing strategic partners and other invited industry guests are expected to attend. The Event will take place at the factory where Cymat produces its Stabilized Aluminum Foam ("SAF"), and the Company is pleased to welcome its guests to see the production facility first-hand. Event attendance is subject to change. Cymat Technologies Ltd. holds the global rights, through patents and established know-how, to manufacture and sell Stabilized Aluminum Foam ("SAF"), a unique, ultra-light, cellular metallic material. The proprietary production process entails the injection of gases through a molten bath of alloyed aluminum infused with ceramic particles. The result is an advanced, lightweight, recyclable material that exhibits unique characteristics including customizable density and dimensions; mechanical energy absorption; thermal and acoustic insulation; and time, temperature and strain-rate insensitivity. A key benefit of this continuous foam production process is its scalability and resultant low cost of production.

items.title: What are Ward 5 Mississauga council election candidates promising for Malton’s future?
items.summary: Candidates outline how they intend to address underinvestment in Ward 5, community safety and better services. (Left to right) Rosemarie Sanchez Sanchez, Michael Anthony Perretta, Natalie Hart, Jamie Dookie, Mandeep Singh Dhaliwal, Ismail Bawa and Aruna Anand at the Oct. 16 Ward 5 candidates meeting. Underinvestment in Malton’s community resources, property standards enforcement, and neighbourhood policing are dominating candidate discussions in Mississauga’s Ward 5 ahead of the municipal election on Oct. 26. On Oct. 16, seven of 10 Ward 5 candidates attended a public meeting organized by Peel Condominium Corp. 33, providing residents an opportunity to hear what Ward 5 contenders — Aruna Anand, Ismail Bawa, Jamie Dookie, Mandeep Singh Dhaliwal, Natalie Hart, Michael Anthony Perretta and Rosemarie Sanchez Sanchez — intend to do, if elected as local councillor. Mississauga News also sent candidates questions about local issues. Responses to those questions and statements made at the candidates’ meeting have been compiled to reflect their positions on several community issues. Responses have been edited for length and clarity where necessary. “My goal for Malton is to build a safe neighbourhood where anyone and everyone feels like they belong in the community, and have pride in their homes,” Anand said in an email. At the candidate forum, she called housing affordability a living crisis, noting Malton’s proximity to Pearson Airport makes it a key arrival point for newcomers. Her priorities focus on leveraging airport expansion for local jobs and transit investments, improving street lighting to reduce crime, expanding youth employment initiatives and establishing local police station office hours for residents.

items.title: Intergenerational Fairness Debate Erupts Over Tedjo's Senior Property-Tax Freeze Proposal
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Mississauga mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo's proposal to permanently freeze property tax increases for seniors has become a flashpoint in a municipal election already centred on affordability. According to the outlet, opponents argue the plan would shift the cost of running city services onto younger property owners already struggling with heavy mortgages. The Star reports Tedjo pointed to a similar program in British Columbia as his inspiration, though that program has drawn criticism for benefiting seniors who don't actually need the assistance and has become a provincial election issue there. According to the outlet, Tedjo said his version would aim to strike the right balance, helping cash-poor seniors stay in their homes without burdening young taxpayers, and noted that he has young children of his own. The Star reports mayoral rival Dipika Damerla called the proposal misleading, warning it could fuel intergenerational unfairness unless it were targeted specifically at low-income seniors. According to the outlet, Trent University municipal finance expert Harry Kitchen offered a blunt assessment of the proposal's feasibility.

items.title: Car Insurance ON Mississauga
items.summary: In 2026, the average car insurance premium in Mississauga is $3,078 per year (about $257 per month). 02% higher than the provincial average of $2,653. This makes Mississauga 173rd out of 181 Ontario communities for car insurance affordability. As of July 1, 2026 in Ontario, some previously mandatory accident benefits are now optional. ca data, drivers in Mississauga pay about $3,078 per year for auto insurance as of March 2026. Drivers here pay premiums that are higher than in Burlington, which is the cheapest city for car insurance in the GTA at $2,109 per year. However, insurance costs in Mississauga are lower relative to the premiums in Brampton, the most expensive city in the region at $3,802 per year. 2% higher. Car insurance premiums depend on many factors, such as the number of claims in an area, the amount of time drivers spend on the road, and each driver’s personal and insurance history. The lowest average premium in Mississauga is found in the L5K area, where drivers pay $2,737 annually. Meanwhile, drivers in L4T have the highest average premiums at $3,937 per year.

items.title: Food Bank Visits Top Half a Million for Second Straight Year Even as Mississauga's Thanksgiving Drive Sets a Fundraising Record
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Food Banks Mississauga's 2026 Thanksgiving campaign raised $857,029, a new record for the drive even though it fell short of its $900,000 goal. According to the outlet, the drive, sponsored by Keurig Dr Pepper Canada, wrapped up Tuesday as the organization marked its 40th anniversary while continuing to face historically high demand across the city. The outlet reports Food Banks Mississauga's network of more than 60 food programs has logged more than half a million visits for a second consecutive year, with the organization estimating someone visits a city food bank every 22 seconds while programs are open. Insauga.com reports the Thanksgiving funds will help keep those programs stocked with fresh and shelf-stable food close to where residents live. According to the outlet, CEO Meghan Nicholls said people turn to food banks for reasons ranging from low wages and high rent to illness, disability or a job that ended, adding that while circumstances vary, the need stays the same. The outlet reports Nicholls credited community donations with letting the organization keep providing relief even as visit numbers remain exceptionally high.

items.title: Cannabis Stop in Mississauga's North End Leads Police to a Loaded Glock and Fentanyl, Police Say
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a traffic stop in Mississauga's north end over an alleged cannabis violation led police to a loaded handgun and a stash of hard drugs. According to police, officers with the force's 11 Division Community Incident Response Team stopped a vehicle near Maritz Drive and Derry Road West, one block west of Hurontario Street, on Oct. 5. Police say the stop began after an alleged Cannabis Control Act violation drew their attention to the vehicle, and officers soon located suspected drugs inside during their investigation. The outlet reports two suspects were arrested and charged following that discovery. According to police, a subsequent search of the car turned up a loaded 9mm Glock handgun fitted with a prohibited 15-round magazine. Police say officers also seized more than 79 grams of suspected drugs, including fentanyl, heroin, crack cocaine and crystal methamphetamine, along with $1,260 in Canadian cash.

items.title: 2,200 Mississauga Aerospace Jobs Hang on Trump's Shifting Stance Toward Bombardier
items.summary: Insauga.com reports U.S. President Donald Trump appears to be stepping back from his threat to block Bombardier aircraft sales in the United States, a shift that could ease concerns for the company's major Mississauga operations. According to the outlet, Trump signalled the change during a rally in Kansas on Monday, saying he would help the Canadian aircraft maker after learning more about its American workforce. Insauga.com reports Trump told the crowd he always viewed Bombardier as a Canadian company and added that the United States would not hurt it given its operations in Kansas, saying he would take care of those jobs. The outlet says the apparent reversal follows a September threat in which Trump declared Bombardier should no longer be allowed to sell its products in the U.S. unless it moved production there. According to insauga.com, that threat had raised concerns about the Quebec-based manufacturer's operations on both sides of the border, including its aircraft assembly centre at Toronto Pearson International Airport in Mississauga. The outlet reports the facility employs more than 2,200 people and sits on a 40-acre campus that includes a 770,000-square-foot final assembly building and a pre-flight hangar, according to the Ontario government.

items.title: Cover your plants: Frost advisory issued in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: Take preventive measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees and crops, Environment Canada says. Environment and Climate Change Canada issues a frost advisory and is warning residents to cover up sensitive plants. It’s been a sunny and warm week across most of southern Ontario, but a chilly evening looms on Tuesday. Environment and Climate Change Canada has issued a yellow level frost advisory for Mississauga and Brampton, warning residents that patchy frost is expected tonight, mainly in areas away from Lake Ontario. The frost advisory extends to St. Catharines, Grimsby and Northern Niagara. According to Environment Canada, frost can potentially cause damage to plants, trees and crops. The cold temperatures impact leaves, flowers and buds still developing on stems. Gardeners can use plastic containers, sheets or bags to cover up their outdoor plants overnight.
